source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Exodus 32–34.

key_decisions.decision: Retains impatient demand, distancing this Moses, and plural divine designation supported by plural verb; no invented motive beyond stated delay.
Retains Aaron’s manufacture and collective acclamation; takes difficult tool expression as engraving and preserves plural declaration despite single calf.
Preserves two offering types and meal-to-revelry sequence; does not add specific sexual acts to broad play verb.
Keeps requested nonintervention, destructive anger, and alternative nation promised to Moses without softening judgment.
Distinguishes Egyptians’ attributed evil intent from threatened disaster while retaining lethal content and explicit appeal to relent.
Retains narrative assertion of relenting without doctrinal paraphrase and keeps his people after the speech exchange.
Preserves three-part sound contrast as lineated speech within verse paragraph and identifies Moses from dialogue context.
Retains every destructive and bodily action in order without inventing calf construction or reducing forced drinking to metaphor.
Preserves Aaron’s implausible account as reported speech, retaining its contrast with his deliberate craftsmanship in verse 4.
Takes unrestrained sense of para rather than inserting nakedness; retains Aaron’s agency and hostile outsiders’ scorn.
Retains Moses’ attribution to the LORD, sword command, traversal and lethal commands against close relationships without euphemism.
Preserves approximate count, male victims, Levites’ action, and narrator’s fell image without reducing deaths to generic casualties.
Renders fill-hands consecration idiom with imperative force; retains compressed kinship cost and blessing without claiming every Levite killed his own son.
Retains great-sin repetition and perhaps uncertainty; preserves atonement term rather than promising certain forgiveness.
Leaves first conditional plea unfinished as in Hebrew and retains Moses’ request for personal erasure without identifying an unstated book of life.
Keeps guidance promise alongside deferred reckoning and repeats visitation idiom as call to account rather than erasing accountability.
Keeps plague and deliberately repeated shared responsibility of people and Aaron instead of harmonizing one away.
